changes.text: 讲稿中有一段关于沉默。富兰克林说，他对宪法缺点的意见，已为公共利益而放弃，从未在外面透露一个字：“它们在这几面墙里产生，也将在这里消亡。”他的意思是：他自己的异议留在会议室内。

One passage of the speech is about silence. Franklin said the opinions he had held of the Constitution's errors he sacrificed to the public good, and had never whispered a syllable of them abroad: "Within these walls they were born, and here they shall die." His point: his own objections would stay in the chamber.

会议官方日志及其他文件的去向也值得留意，它们和本篇所依据的麦迪逊笔记是两份不同的材料。同日的笔记里，金建议销毁会议日志或交主席保管，理由是日志若公开，会被想阻挠宪法的人利用；威尔逊倾向交主席保管（他一度更赞成销毁），说虚假说法可能流传，不应让反驳无从谈起；最终决定把日志及其他文件交主席保管，听候日后若依宪法成立的国会处置。至于富兰克林关于太阳的那段话，笔记记的是他望着椅背，对身边几位成员说的——那是对身边几个人说的话，不是对全场的正式演说。另外，本篇只写到1787年9月17日会议散会为止，不涉及宪法此后的批准与修正。

The fate of the Convention's official Journals and other papers also deserves a look; they are a different set of papers from the Madison notes this piece relies on. In Madison's notes for the same day, King suggests that the Journals be destroyed or left in the president's custody, since made public they would be put to bad use by those wishing to prevent the Constitution's adoption; Wilson prefers the second course, though he had at one time liked the first best — false suggestions may be spread, and it should not be made impossible to contradict them — and the Journals and other papers are left with the president, subject to the order of Congress, if ever formed under the Constitution. As for Franklin and the sun, the notes record that he observed to a few members near him: an aside to those beside him, not a formal address to the whole hall. In any case, this piece stops at the adjournment of 17 September 1787 and touches neither ratification nor amendment.

dispositions.rationale: I changed the evaluative opening "最硬的一段/The hardest passage" to the neutral "讲稿中有一段关于沉默/One passage of the speech is about silence". I rewrote the final sentence so it is attributed to Franklin's own position: "他的意思是：他自己的异议留在会议室内/His point: his own objections would stay in the chamber." The evidence only supports Franklin's statement that his own objections had not been spread outside the chamber. It does not support a general claim about everything said in the chamber.

evidence.quote: I have never whispered a syllable of them abroad. Within these walls they were born, and here they shall die.

dispositions.rationale: I rewrote the opening sentence to make clear that the papers handed to the presiding officer were the convention's official Journals and other papers. I also stated that these are a different body of material from the Madison notes this piece relies on. In the Chinese, "会议记录" is changed throughout to "会议日志". The English now consistently says Journals and makes clear that the discussion is recorded in Madison's notes for the same day.

evidence.quote: Mr. KING suggested that the Journals of the Convention should be either destroyed, or deposited in the custody of the president.
A question was then put on depositing the Journals, and other papers of the Convention, in the hands of the president
